Article Title: SC upholds Karnataka HC order to allow bike taxis, rejects state govt's challenge
Article Text:
SC dismisses Karnataka's appeal against HC order allowing bike taxi services in State

NEW DELHI: In a setback to the Karnataka government, the Supreme Court on Friday refused to interfere with a state high court ruling that permits bike taxi services to operate across Karnataka.A bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N Kotiswar Singh dismissed the state's appeal, thereby retaining the relief granted to bike taxi aggregators and operators by the Karnataka High Court, news agency ANI reported.The case dates back to an earlier order that had asked bike taxi operators to halt services until the state introduced a regulatory framework. However, on January 23, 2026, a division bench of the high court, then headed by Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and comprising Justice CM Joshi, overturned that direction.The high court's ruling came on appeals by Ola , Uber, Rapido, motorcycle owners and the Bike Taxi Welfare Association. It said motorcycles could be registered as transport vehicles and used as contract carriages, provided they complied with the state's regulatory requirements.The state government subsequently approached the apex court, arguing that the operation of bike taxis raised concerns about passenger safety, insurance protection and the absence of adequate safeguards.Traditional auto and taxi driver associations had also opposed the move, contending that bike taxi operators should not be allowed to function without meeting regulatory obligations comparable to those imposed on conventional transport services.
Article Summary: Supreme Court refuses to interfere with state high court ruling that permits bike taxi services to operate across Karnataka. Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N Kotiswar Singh dismissed the state's appeal. Case dates back to an earlier order that had asked bike taxi operators to halt services until the state introduced a regulatory framework.

Article Title: US court to Delhi courts: Help serve summons to R&AW ex-chief, Doval
Article Text:
NSA Ajit Doval (File photo)

US court move a 'procedural, routine' step

NEW DELHI: A US district court has ordered alternative delivery of summons through Indian courts on NSA Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing chief Samant Goel. However, sources said the summons was not binding.The Clerk of the US Court has been directed to send the necessary judicial documents via international mail or courier to three district courts in Delhi - Patiala House, Dwarka and Tis Hazari district courts.The order was issued by Judge Katherine Polk Failla of the court of Southern District of New York in a civil lawsuit filed by Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, founder of pro-Khalistan outfit Sikhs for Justice (SFJ).“The court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court,” says an order by a US district court, seeking to serve summons on Ajit Doval and Samant Goel.The order states that standard service through India's central authority under the Hague Convention was attempted but rejected. The court then authorised alternative service under Article 19 of the Hague Convention and India's Code of Civil Procedure.Sources described the move as a “routine, procedural step”. Earlier, the summons was delivered through the Indian embassy by the US State Department, which had clarified that this did not reflect any position on the case.In 2013, former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh was served with a civil summons in a suit filed by SFJ, alleging human rights violations related to the 1984 riots.
Article Summary: US court move a 'procedural, routine' step, sources say. Move follows a civil lawsuit filed by Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, founder of pro-Khalistan outfit Sikhs for Justice. In 2013, former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh was served with a civil summons in a suit filed by SFJ.

NEW DELHI: Signaling deepening political fault lines in the parliamentary committee scrutinising the contentious FCRA bill, several opposition MPs have flagged the manner in which objections against the proposed law from different stakeholders were being processed and claimed their own questions and subsequent replies were not being adequately recorded.The joint committee of Parliament headed by BJP's Sanjay Jaiswal met on Thursday to deliberate over the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, with opposition MPs including P Wilson and A Raja of DMK, Christopher Manickam of Congress and Menaka Guruswamy of TMC recording their objections in writing to him.Jaiswal, however, said minutes of the meeting were being given to members and verbatim details of the proceedings, too, will be sent to them. He had already agreed to their request for four weeks to be given to allow all interested stakeholders to submit their views, the Lok Sabha MP said, suggesting that it may not be feasible to keep pushing back the duration.In their letter, opposition members said, "The proceedings of the committee, particularly the questions raised by members and the corresponding replies and clarifications provided by other members and witnesses are not being adequately and accurately recorded in the minutes of the meetings.Such omissions may result in an incomplete account and do not appear to be in keeping with the established principles and practices governing parliamentary proceedings. "Representations made different stakeholders were also not treated on equal footing, they claimed.Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, which seeks to regulate foreign donations , is being bitterly opposed by opposition parties and Christian bodies. While Congress and other opposition parties have called it unconstitutional, Christian organisations have said it will hamper their charitable work. Several RSS-affiliated bodies have, however, claimed that the law is needed to stop funneling of foreign money for conversion.
Article Summary: Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, is being bitterly opposed by opposition parties and Christian bodies. Congress and other opposition parties have called it unconstitutional, Christian organisations have said it will hamper their charitable work. Several RSS-affiliated bodies have, however, claimed that the law is needed to stop funneling of foreign money for conversion.

Article Title: BJP cites Moily remark to claim Congress tried to 'frame' PM Modi

NEW DELHI: Congress leader M Veerappa Moily has claimed PM Narendra Modi would have gone to jail when he was CM of Gujarat but the probe against him was stalled by some Congress members when the party was in office; comments cited by BJP as vindication of its charge that Modi was being targeted as part of political vendetta.Moily's comment acquires significance in light of speculation in political circles before 2014 LS polls that Modi and Amit Shah could be arrested in Ishrat Jahan case."The mask has completely fallen off," BJP spokesman Sudhanshu Trivedi said, adding that Moily's statement suggested that investigating agencies and judicial processes were "completely sidelined" under Congress govt, which tried to "frame" Modi, and demanded a response from the opposition party.Speaking at the release of Sonia Gandhi's memoir at Congress office in Bengaluru, Moily said Shah had gone to jail and was externed, and claimed that he would not have become the powerful home minister that he is now. Shah was arrested in Sohrabuddin Sheikh fake encounter case. He was later discharged.Moily, a cabinet minister in UPA govt, said, "The next would have been Modi to go inside (jail). The investigation against Narendra Modi was stalled.(By) our own govt, not because of Manmohan Singh (then PM) but some other leaders. We are suffering because of that today."BJP said Moily's remarks made it clear that Congress tried to "frame" Modi and Shah and all allegations levelled against them back then were "politically motivated".It is clear how much respect they have for the Constitution, Trivedi said. "It has become clear that the allegations levelled against Modi and Shah were manufactured by Congress and were politically motivated," he added.Trivedi said another conclusion from Moily's remark was that "person in charge" wasn't Manmohan Singh. "Congress must now address this; there is no room left for doubt. The mask has fallen off. It is clear that someone else was calling the shots."

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Team of lawyer comrades are in touch with them.But if any lawyer can be at the PS immediately, pls DM."Rosie is among the three female journalists who filed complaint alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3.The complants have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action.Delhi Police also detained several protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating over an alleged incident of sexual misconduct involving three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.The protesters alleged that they had been demonstrating since 6pm on Sunday, demanding registration of an FIR in the case. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. Article Title: Boyfriend of woman who fell to death from hotel 'dies by suicide' in Lucknow jail
Article Text:
Avnish Jaiswal, accused of causing his girlfriend Samreen's death, was found dead in jail

‘Avnish was pressuring her to marry him’





LUCKNOW: A 30-year-old man arrested for the death of his girlfriend, who fell from the 10th floor of a hotel on Oct 12, allegedly died by suicide in Lucknow jail on Thursday.Avnish Jaiswal alias Dev was found hanging from a towel in the jail bathroom. He had been lodged there since Oct 15.DG (Prisons) PC Meena suspended jail warder and barrack in-charge Hari Om and initiated departmental proceedings against him for negligence. Departmental action is also being initiated against head jail warders Dev Prakash Singh, Uday Narayan and Deependra Singh.Jailor Ritwik Priyadarshi told TOI that Avnish was depressed and had told fellow inmates that he was unable to come to terms with the death of Samreen (24).Samreen died after falling from the 10th floor of a hotel in Gomti Nagar Extension.She had been staying with Avnish when the incident occurred. Samreen’s family had alleged that Avnish was pressuring her to marry him and pushed her off the building after she refused. The family also alleged that he fled the hotel on a motorcycle after the incident. Police registered a murder case against Avnish following a complaint by Samreen’s sister. He surrendered before an ACJM court on Oct 15 and was sent to judicial custody
Article Summary: Avnish Jaiswal alias Dev was found hanging from a towel in the jail bathroom. He had been lodged there since Oct 15. Samreen died after falling from the 10th floor of a hotel in Gomti Nagar Extension. She had been staying with Avnish when the incident occurred.

Article Title: AAP councillor loses MCD seat over concealing 2013 conviction, BJP rival gets ward
Article Text: New Delhi: Concealing his conviction in the poll affidavit has cost AAP councillor Arun Nawariya his MCD seat from Pushp Vihar ward 166, with a court setting aside his election in the 2022 polls and declaring BJP candidate Naresh , who finished second, the winner.The court held that hiding his criminal record amounted to a corrupt electoral practice and deprived voters of their right to make an informed choice. Declaring Nawariya’s election null and void, principal district and sessions judge Sanjeev Kumar Aggarwal observed that voters have a right to know about the criminal antecedents of candidates they are electing as their representatives.Nawariya had adopted a corrupt practice by concealing his conviction under Section 325 (voluntarily causing grievous hurt) of Indian Penal Code in a 2010 case.Naresh had challenged Nawariya’s election, alleging that the latter deliberately concealed his 2013 conviction in the mandatory nomination affidavit.The court found that Nawariya had filled in ‘Not Applicable’ against the column in Form 22 seeking details of criminal cases, despite having been convicted in the case and released on probation after furnishing a bond for good behaviour.Nawariya’s defence argued that the conviction did not involve moral turpitude and, therefore, could not be a ground to declare his election void.It also contended that Form 22 sought additional information about criminal cases beyond what was required under Rule 18 of Delhi Municipal Corporation Election of Councillors Rules, 2012.Rejecting the arguments, the court noted that Nawariya had not challenged the validity of Form 22 before any competent authority or court and had himself submitted his nomination affidavit in the prescribed format.The court added that the disclosure requirements were intended to make municipal elections “more fair and transparent” and applied equally to all candidates. It held that Nawariya was bound to disclose his conviction, irrespective of the nature of the sentence imposed.Holding his election null and void, the court ruled that Naresh, having secured the second-highest number of votes, was entitled to be declared the elected councillor from the ward.Welcoming the court’s decision, Delhi BJP spokesperson Praveen Shankar Kapoor said, “The court has rightfully declared BJP candidate Naresh, who finished second, as the councillor from ward 166 with immediate effect.” He also appreciated advocates Swastik Singh and Atul Singh for their efforts.
Article Summary: Nawariya had adopted a corrupt practice by concealing his conviction under Section 325 (voluntarily causing grievous hurt) of Indian Penal Code in a 2010 case. Naresh had challenged Nawariya’s election, alleging that the latter deliberately concealed his 2013 conviction in the mandatory nomination affidavit.

Article Title: Ex-Sena MLA Shrinivas Vanga returns to BJP
Article Text: Palghar: Former Palghar MLA Shrinivas Vanga rejoined BJP on Thursday, ending a long phase of political uncertainty.Vanga, son of the late BJP MP Chintaman Vanga, had quit the party after being denied a ticket for the Palghar Lok Sabha bypoll following his father’s death. He joined the undivided Shiv Sena and won the 2019 Assembly election from Palghar. After the Sena split, he backed Eknath Shinde and was among the MLAs who travelled to Guwahati.However, Vanga was upset after the Shinde-led Sena denied him a ticket in 2024. He had broken down before cameras, later alleging injustice, and stayed away from active politics.He joined BJP at a sports event in Palghar in the presence of party district president Ravindra Chavan.
Article Summary: Vanga, son of the late BJP MP Chintaman Vanga, had quit the party after being denied a ticket for the Palghar Lok Sabha bypoll following his father’s death. He joined the undivided Shiv Sena and won the 2019 Assembly election. He had broken down before cameras, later alleging injustice, and stayed away from active politics.

Article Title: Ashok Chavan criticises Rohit Pawar for targeting Fadnavis
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





BJP MP and former Maharashtra chief minister Ashok Chavan on Thursday hit out at NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar over his allegations against chief minister Devendra Fadnavis in connection with the plane crash that killed deputy CM Ajit Pawar .Calling Pawar’s allegations “baseless”, Chavan questioned his political intent. “It appears Rohit Pawar is in a hurry to establish himself as a political leader,” Chavan told reporters in Nanded .Pawar had accused Fadnavis of shielding the airline involved in the crash. Chavan rejected the charge.In a separate political departure from his party’s stand, Chavan said he would read Congress politician Sonia Gandhi ’s autobiography, ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’, despite BJP opposing the book.Chavan, who spent more than four decades in Congress before joining BJP, said his long association with the party made him curious about Gandhi’s account.“I was in Congress for several years, so I should know what happened during that period,” he said.“Sonia Gandhi has witnessed several ups and downs in her political and personal life, and the book recounts those experiences. There is nothing beyond that,” he said.Asked about BJP protests in which copies of the book were torn, Chavan struck a cautious note. He said everyone had their own perspective and took positions accordingly, but declined to comment further.BJP has accused Gandhi of using the autobiography to gloss over mistakes made during Congress govts. Party workers have protested against the book at several places.
Article Summary: Former Maharashtra chief minister Ashok Chavan hit out at NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar over his allegations against chief minister Devendra Fadnavis. Chavan questioned Pawar’s political intent, saying he was in a hurry to establish himself as a political leader. In a separate political departure from his party's stand, Chavan said he would read Congress politician Sonia Gandhi ’s autobiography.

Article Title: Farmers stage road blockade in Beed
Article Text:
Farmers during their protest outside Chousala bus stand in Beed taluka on Thursday

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Farmers staged a road blockade outside the Chousala bus stand on Thursday, protesting alleged harassment, financial exploitation and intimidation by wind energy companies operating in the Balaghat hill range in Beed taluka. The protesters alleged that farmers opposing the companies’ activities were being threatened with extortion cases to silence them.The farmers alleged that wind energy companies were installing electricity poles and laying transmission lines through agricultural land without obtaining the consent of landowners. They also accused the companies of denying farmers adequate compensation and, in some cases, issuing cheques that could not be encashed, thereby causing financial losses.Organised by the Shetkari Hakka Morcha, the agitation saw farmers from Chousala, Kanadighat, Golangri, Malewadi, Borkhed, Ghargaon, Ruigavhan, Wadwadi and Babhalgaon express anger against the functioning of windmill companies in their areas.They raised slogans demanding an end to alleged high-handedness and exploitation by the companies and condemning the revenue and police administrations for allegedly protecting them.The farmers further alleged that those opposing such work were subjected to threats and intimidation, including threats of being booked in extortion cases. They also claimed that land acquisition activities were being carried out illegally with the alleged connivance of certain officials from the revenue and police departments.After the protest, the farmers submitted a memorandum through the district collector to chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde and guardian minister Sunetra Pawar.Beed tehsildar Chandrakant Shelke and Neknoor police station assistant inspector Mangesh Salve received the memorandum. Police sub-inspectors and personnel from Neknoor police station were also present.Ganesh Dhawale, who raised the issue during the agitation, said the state industries, energy and labour department had issued a govt resolution on Oct 21, 2013, providing for district, taluka and sub-divisional monitoring committees for wind energy projects.“Despite the committees being constituted, their functioning is not effective. Farmers have repeatedly approached the administration with complaints but have failed to get justice. This has emboldened the companies to continue their alleged exploitation and harassment,” Dhawale said.
Article Summary: Farmers staged a road blockade outside the Chousala bus stand in Beed taluka. They are protesting alleged harassment, financial exploitation and intimidation by wind energy companies operating in the Balaghat hill range. The protesters alleged that farmers opposing the companies’ activities were being threatened with extortion cases to silence them.

NAVI MUMBAI: A 25-year-old woman on Monday lodged a rape complaint at CBD-Belapur police station against habitual offender Shailendra Dwivedi (50), who allegedly posed as a journalist.Dwivedi was arrested by Ulwe police on November 12 in a cheating and criminal breach of trust case for allegedly duping Thane trader Vijay Jha and four others of Rs 19 lakh in a flat sale deal. Article Title: Shiv Sena’s focus is on improving its base in Pune ahead of 2029 elections, not to challenge other parties, says party senior & minister Uday Samant
Article Text:
Uday Samant

Pune:





State industries minister and Shiv Sena senior Uday Samant on Thursday said the party would work towards strengthening its base in the district with a view to the 2029 elections.Samant’s comment came against the backdrop of Shiv Sena’s decision to support a rebel candidate against BJP’s official nominee for the Pune teachers’ constituency in the recently concluded state MLC polls. Clarifying his party’s stand, Samant said, “Shiv Sena is not challenging any party, but is looking to grow its base in Pune.”Along with Legislative Council deputy chairperson Sachin Ahir, Samant held a series of meetings with party functionaries in Baramati, Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) and Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) limits on Thursday.The outreach assumes significance as Shiv Sena failed to win a single seat in last year’s PMC elections. Following the poor showing, the party reorganised its local unit and entrusted Samant with the task of rebuilding its organisation in the region.Addressing party workers after the meetings, Samant indicated further restructuring of local units in the coming months. “The Shiv Sena chief has given me the responsibility to grow the party in Baramati, Pune and Pimpri Chinchwad. While we are looking to expand our party’s base, we will continue to work unitedly in Mahayuti,” Samant said.The meetings form part of the party’s broader strategy to expand its footprint in western Maharashtra while maintaining its alliance with Mahayuti partners.
Article Summary: State industries minister and Shiv Sena senior Uday Samant said the party would work towards strengthening its base in the district with a view to the 2029 elections. Samant’s comment came against the backdrop of Shiv Sen a decision to support a rebel candidate in the recently concluded state MLC polls.

Article Title: Congress demands FIR, independent probe into Bhusawal voter objections
Article Text:
Harshwardhan Sapkal

Nashik:





A total of 183 people filed objections against the names of 14,567 electors in the Bhusawal assembly constituency in Jalgaon district, prompting the district election office to verify the claims.However, the Congress has questioned the process irrespective of its outcome, demanding an FIR and a thorough inquiry into who filed the objections and how bulk applications were permitted in an alleged attempt to delete eligible voters.While the district election office stated that verification by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) found all entries genuine except those of 74 deceased electors, Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal demanded strict action against those involved.“The state Election Commission has been urged to order an independent inquiry into this matter, immediately register an FIR, and take strict action against all those responsible, including the masterminds behind it. No attempt to deprive voters of their rights will be tolerated,” Sapkal wrote in a post on X.The Congress has alleged that the objections were filed in a coordinated manner, with some applications submitted in the names of people who later denied filing them. It has sought an independent, time-bound inquiry by officials from outside Jalgaon district, along with action against those responsible for preparing and accepting the applicationsCongress city president Ahmed Qureshi and party members objected to the Form-7 claims raised by the 183 unverified citizens before the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) of Bhusawal.“We are unable to understand how 183 applicants raised objections to 14,567 names in a single day when an individual can file only 10 applications. This is a perfect example showing that BJP people are trying their ways and means to delete the names of people who are not in their favour,” claimed Qureshi.Congress district president Dhananjay Chaudhari said party workers met some applicants who were unaware of objections filed in their names. “The people against whom objections were filed were genuine as claimed by the administration. However, this does not solve our issue. The administration should conduct a thorough inquiry to find out who filed the objections using CCTV footage, and file an FIR against them,” demanded Chaudhari, warning of strong agitation in the event of failure.Electoral registration officer Jitendra Patil said, “The objections were filed through ‘inward’ in the office and hence had to be attended to as per Election Commission of India norms. Booth Level Officers thoroughly checked them, and we found only 74 names of electors who had died some time back. All other names are safe.”
Article Summary: A total of 183 people filed objections against the names of 14,567 electors in the Bhusawal assembly constituency in Jalgaon district. The district election office stated that verification by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) found all entries genuine except those of 74 deceased electors. Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal demanded strict action against those involved.

Article Title: Police file chargesheet against Kayalvizhi Alagiri in SBI manager assault case
Article Text:
Chennai:





Adyar police filed the chargesheet against Kayalvizhi Alagiri, daughter of former Union minister M K Alagiri, before IX Metropolitan Magistrate Court in Saidapet in connection with the alleged assault of a State Bank of India (SBI) branch manager at the bank’s NRI branch in Adyar. The court took the case on file on Thursday and scheduled the next hearing for Dec 22, 2026.The case arose from an incident on July 20, when Harshin Singh, manager of the SBI branch, raised concerns about a malfunctioning lift in the commercial building owned by Kayalvizhi. Police said repeated requests to the building’s representatives to repair the lift remained unresolved, after which Singh contacted her directly.Investigators said Kayalvizhi later visited the bank and an argument broke out over the issue. She assaulted and threatened the manager. The incident was captured on the bank’s CCTV cameras, and the footage later circulated on social media.Based on a complaint lodged by Namachivayam, chief manager of SBI Regional Business Office-II, Adyar police registered a case under sections 296(b), 329(4), 115(2) and 351(2) of the BNS.Kayalvizhi appeared before the investigating officer after receiving a summons, was questioned for about two hours, formally arrested and released on station bail. The case will proceed before the Saidapet court.
Article Summary: Adyar police filed chargesheet against Kayalvizhi Alagiri, daughter of former Union minister. Alleged assault of State Bank of India branch manager at the bank’s NRI branch in Adyar. Court took the case on file on Thursday and scheduled the next hearing for Dec 22, 2026.

Article Title: Rash and wrong-side driving: Coimbatore district police book driver, seize private bus, recommend cancellation of licence and permit
Article Text:

COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore district police have seized a private mofussil bus and booked its driver for rash, negligent and wrong-side driving at Pappampatti Pirivu on the Coimbatore–Palladam Road.According to a statement issued by the district police on Tuesday, the incident occurred around 8.30am on Monday while the private bus was heading to Coimbatore from Tirupur. Near Pappampatti Pirivu, which falls under the Sulur police station limits, driver Sakthivel drove the bus at a high speed before abruptly swerving the vehicle to the right and driving against the oncoming traffic on the wrong side of the busy stretch, putting motorists and pedestrians at a grave risk.Several commuters recorded the dangerous manoeuvre and uploaded the footage online, where it quickly gained widespread traction. Acting on a formal complaint lodged by a motorist, the Sulur police registered a case against Sakthivel under Section 281 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) read with Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act Police impounded the bus and parked it on the Sulur police station premises for further legal proceedings. Additionally, authorities have written to the regional transport officer recommending the cancellation of Sakthivel’s driving licence as well as the vehicle’s route permit.Reiterating a zero-tolerance stance, the district police warned that strict legal action would be taken against motorists endangering public safety.
Article Summary: The Coimbatore district police seized a private mofussil bus and booked its driver for rash, negligent and wrong-side driving. Driver Sakthivel drove the bus at a high speed before abruptly swerving the vehicle to the right and driving against the oncoming traffic.

Article Title: Verdict on Sulur minor girl rape-murder case postponed to Nov 27
Article Text: COIMBATORE: A special court for Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act cases on Monday postponed to Nov 27 its verdict on the rape and murder of a 10-year-old girl near Sulur in Coimbatore district.The verdict was scheduled to be pronounced on Monday by judge Hariharan. No specific reason was stated for the postponement.On May 21, a 10-year-old girl from Pallapalayam near Sulur went missing after visiting a local shop. Her body was found the next day near the Kannampalayam lakebed. Police arrested K Karthi,35, and R Mohan, 31, both of whom were residing in the same locality.Police registered a case under sections 5(m), 5(i), 6(1), 5(I), 5(j)(iv), 16 and 17 of the POCSO Act and 103(1), 61(2)(a), 140(1), 140(4), 238(a), 127(2), 65, 49, 240, 249(a) of the BNS. The first hearing of the case took place on June 10. Prime accused Karthi was lodged in Madurai Central Prison, while Mohan was lodged in Trichy Central Prison.On Monday, both were produced before the court. While police were bringing them to the court, Mohan asked the media people not to take video of him, claiming that police had falsely included him in the case.
Article Summary: The verdict was scheduled to be pronounced on Monday by judge Hariharan. No specific reason was stated for the postponement. On May 21, a 10-year-old girl from Pallapalayam near Sulur went missing after visiting a local shop. Her body was found the next day near the Kannampalayan lakebed.

A 54-year-old man was arrested by forest protection squad officials for possessing leopard claws near Sathyamangalam on Saturday evening.He was apprehended when a special team conducted a patrol along the Sathyamangalam–Athani Road, following a tip-off. During the operation, officials noticed a man standing alone under suspicious circumstances near the Hospital Medu bus stop. “A subsequent search of the suspect led to the recovery of two leopard claws,” said a forest officer.The man was identified as Shanmugam, 54, of Kuttai Thottam, in Sathyamangalam taluk. He was taken to the Sathyamangalam forest range office for further interrogation.A wildlife offense case was subsequently registered against him. The accused and the seized claws were produced before the judicial magistrate in Sathyamangalam on Saturday night. Further investigation is on.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.

Article Title: Central crime branch probes illegal quarrying cases, searches TN former minister P Moorthy's house
Article Text:
TN former minister P Moorthy





MADURAI: Madurai district police conducted a search on Friday at the residence of former minister P Moorthy in connection with two cases of alleged illegal quarrying involving the extraction of minerals beyond permitted limits, causing substantial losses to the government.According to officials, a quarry lessee at Sathiravellalapatti in Vadipatti taluk allegedly excavated gravel stones beyond the sanctioned quantity and from land for which no permission had been obtained. Based on inspections conducted by the Department of Geology and Mining, the Revenue Divisional Officer reported that the alleged violations resulted in losses of Rs 2.32 crore and Rs 3.07 crore to the government in two separate instances.Acting on the complaints, the Madurai District Central Crime Branch registered two cases.As part of the investigation, a police team searched Moorthy's residence on Roja Street in Ezhil Nagar, Iyer Bungalow, after informing the Judicial Magistrate Court.Officials said the search was aimed at identifying documents and other materials related to the alleged illegal quarrying activities. Further investigation is under way.
Article Summary: Madurai district police conducted a search on Friday at the residence of former minister P Moorthy in connection with two cases of alleged illegal quarrying. The alleged violations resulted in losses of Rs 2.32 crore and Rs 3.07 crore to the government in two separate instances.

Article Title: Tonsure fraud: DVAC books temple official, trustees’ chief
Article Text:
Tonsure fraud: DVAC books temple official, trustees’ chief





Madurai: Directorate of vigilance and anti-corruption (DVAC) has registered a case against 10 people, including the assistant commissioner and hereditary trustees’ chairman of Irukkankudi Mariamman temple near Sattur, for an alleged fraud in the free tonsure scheme.A surprise inspection on Nov 17 uncovered an alleged racket involving unauthorised barbers, compulsory collections from devotees and fabricated records to claim govt payments.Those booked include assistant commissioner Ilangovan, hereditary trustees’ chairman M Ramamoorthy, temple guard Singaravelu, office assistant Ganesan, assistant guard-cum-barber Yogarajan and five others.Investigators found that six officially appointed barbers had engaged 28 unauthorised workers to perform tonsures while continuing to receive payments from the temple administration. The workers were allegedly paid daily wages from money collected from devotees instead of being given regular salaries. Under the govt scheme, barbers receive ₹30 for each tonsure, while devotees are entitled to the service free of charge.DVAC also uncovered suspected manipulation of records to claim payments for tonsures never performed. Officials found 55 pre-printed tokens at the counter without corresponding devotees.Tokens were also issued without photographs, violating HR&CE department procedures.During the inspection, officials seized ₹59,520 in unaccounted cash from unauthorised barbers and ₹20,500 from a temple guard. Investigators suspect the alleged fraud, dating back to 2022, could involve several crores of rupees. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A surprise inspection on Nov 17 uncovered an alleged racket involving unauthorised barbers, compulsory collections from devotees and fabricated records. Under the govt scheme, barbers receive ₹30 for each tonsure, while devotees are entitled to the service free of charge. Investigators suspect the alleged fraud, dating back to 2022, could involve several crores of rupees.

Article Title: Doctor arrested for molesting woman patient during check-up
Article Text:
Madurai City South All Women Police have registered a case against a private clinic doctor for sexually harassing the wife of a policeman who went for treatment in Madurai The woman's family staged a protest at Madurai collectorate demanding the arrest of the doctor

An 83-year-old doctor was arrested on Thursday for allegedly sexually harassing a 27-year-old woman during a medical examination at his private clinic in Ponmeni. The arrest was made following a protest by her family at the Madurai collectorate demanding action.The woman, from Virudhunagar district, had travelled to Madurai on Tuesday with her parents and child to consult Durairaj , who had been the family's doctor for years.According to the FIR, the doctor was away when they reached his clinic in the morning. They waited until he arrived in the evening and examined the child for cold and fever.The woman subsequently complained of pain and swelling in her shoulder. The doctor asked her to enter an examination room and instructed her parents to wait outside.She alleged that under the pretext of examining her, the doctor touched her inappropriately despite her hesitation. When he allegedly attempted further inappropriate contact, she pushed him away and rushed out screaming.Her father alerted police through the emergency helpline. Thilagar Thidal all women police station subsequently registered a case under Section 75 of the BNS (sexual harassment) on Tuesday night.However, the family protested at the collectorate on Thursday, alleging that police were reluctant to arrest the doctor. The woman questioned the delay despite lodging a formal complaint. Police subsequently arrested Durairaj.
Article Summary: The woman's family staged a protest at Madurai collectorate demanding the arrest of the doctor. The woman, from Virudhunagar district, had travelled to Madurai on Tuesday with her parents and child to consult Durairaj, who had been the family's doctor for years. The doctor asked her to enter an examination room and instructed her parents to wait outside. She alleged that under the pretext of examining her, the doctor touched her inappropriately.

SALEM: A govt school teacher was arrested in Salem district on Sunday night under sections of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act on charges of inappropriate behaviour towards girl students.The arrested teacher, M Sankar, 49, of Vinayagapuram, is serving as a social science teacher in a govt school in the district.According to the complaint, the teacher allegedly made inappropriate remarks to Class X girl students on Nov 5. “He is accused of making a heart-shaped hand gesture towards one student and calling another student ‘Cleopatra’ while commenting on the beauty of her eyes,” said an officer at the all women police station in Attur.The students brought the matter to the notice of the headmaster on Nov 13. The headmaster informed chief educational officer A Ellappan and contacted Childline 1098 seeking intervention.Following the complaint, a member of the child welfare committee visited the school on Nov 14 and conducted an inquiry into the allegations raised by the students.Based on the findings, the headmaster lodged a complaint with the Attur all women police on Sunday. Police registered a case against Sankar and arrested him. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The arrested teacher, M Sankar, 49, of Vinayagapuram, is serving as a social science teacher in a govt school in the district. He is accused of making a heart-shaped hand gesture towards one student and calling another student ‘Cleopatra’

Article Title: Forest minister convenes emergency meeting after wild elephant herd enters Ranni town
Article Text:
A wild elephant charges towards residents in Ranni on Thursday

Kottayam:





A herd of wild elephants entered Vadasserikkara in Ranni, Pathanamthitta, on Thursday, triggering panic among residents. The herd was reported in the town around noon.Following the incident, forest minister Shibu Baby John convened an emergency online meeting of people’s representatives and senior officials. The minister also directed officials concerned to implement decisions taken at the meeting without delay.Major directions: Parts of the fencing installed around plantations at Attakkuzhi will be removed immediately. More forest department field staff will be deployed in the Vadasserikkara area. Locals experienced in safely driving away wild elephants will be engaged on a temporary basis.The meeting also decided to move in additional rapid response team (RRT) units from other areas. More police personnel will be deployed to ensure the safety of residents and Sabarimala pilgrims.It was also decided that the district collector would issue an order under the Disaster Management Act to regulate pineapple cultivation in the area to remove conditions that attract wild elephants.Pathanamthitta MP Anto Antony, Ranni MLA Pazhakulam Madhu, forest department secretary K Biju, district collector A Nizamuddeen, chief wildlife warden P Pukazhanthi, southern circle CCF Karthikeyan and Ranni DFO Arul Selvan attended the meeting.
Article Summary: Wild elephants entered Vadasserikkara in Ranni, Pathanamthitta, on Thursday, triggering panic among residents. Forest minister Shibu Baby John convened an emergency online meeting of people’s representatives and senior officials. More police personnel will be deployed to ensure the safety of residents and Sabarimala pilgrims.

Article Title: Police job for two bodybuilders: Kerala HC tells DGP to submit files & file notes in sealed cover
Article Text:
AI image

Kochi

:





The high court has directed the state police chief to produce before it, in a sealed cover, the files and file notes relating to the appointment of two bodybuilders as inspectors in the state police by Dec 7.Justice A Badharudeen issued the directive on a petition filed by activist K M Shajahan of Thiruvananthapuram , challenging the govt order denying prior sanction under Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act for a vigilance probe into the appointments of bodybuilders Shinu Chova and Chitharesh Natesan as police inspectors.Shajahan had earlier approached the HC seeking a vigilance probe into the appointments. However, the state govt denied prior sanction for the probe under the Prevention of Corruption Act and informed the court that the appointments had been frozen. The court subsequently disposed of the petition, granting liberty to Shajahan or any other aggrieved person to challenge the govt order denying prior sanction.In his fresh petition challenging the govt order, Shajahan alleged that certain senior police officers had acted with dishonest intent in pursuing the appointments. He further alleged that a second physical efficiency test was conducted for the two bodybuilders after they failed to clear the first test, despite a note by the then Battalion ADGP pointing out that there was no provision for conducting a second test.The petitioner also claimed that the files relating to the appointments had been transferred to the T2 section, which deals with security matters, thereby restricting public access to them under the RTI Act. Seeking production of the files for the court’s scrutiny, he requested the court to call for and examine the records.The bench directed the state police chief to submit the files and file notes in a sealed cover by Dec 7 and issued notice to the respondents.
Article Summary: The high court has directed the state police chief to produce before it, in a sealed cover, the files and file notes relating to the appointment of two bodybuilders as inspectors. Justice A Badharudeen issued the directive on a petition filed by activist K M Shajahan of Thiruvananthapuram. He had earlier approached the HC seeking a vigilance probe into the appointments.
